Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

City Clerk Cornejo reminded City Council of Boards and Commission interviews November 8, 2021.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez announced Holiday program which includes a Tree Lighting ceremony December 11, 2021
between 5-7 pm.

City Manager Gonzalez provided an overview of City Council Special Meeting held on how to allocate 6.7 million dollars
of reserves that the General Fund has.

Council Comments

Mayor Pro-Tem Avila reported that he attended the chamber breakfast on October 20th, and thanked the Chamber of
Commerce for hosting and commended Lieutenant Rocky Wenrick on his presentation at the event. On October 27th, he
attended the luncheon at Veterans park and he thanked the Employee Relations Committee for arranging the event. He
also attended Fall Festival and thanked Azusa City Library for their tremendous efforts in putting the event together.

Mayor Pro-Tem Avila wished Pastor Griffin from Sandals Church a speedy recovery, and thanked Will Yih for stepping
in and performing the invocation.

Councilmember Alvarez reported on the Foothill Transit meeting he attended. Ridership increased by 8% within the past
few months, fares will be reduced, and changes are being proposed to eliminate the Tap card discount and implement
unlimited transfers for 2 hours. He also mentioned that Foothill Transit has noticed an increase in graffiti on their property
and inquired if there was an increase in graffiti or other problems in the parking structures within the City.

In response to questions posed by Council, Chief of Police Bertelsen responded by stating that the Police Department has
increased patrol around the Foothill Transit properties due to the increased graffiti.

Councilmember Alvarez also mentioned that Foothill Transit is missing about 2-3% of their trips due to staffing
shortages.

Councilmember Mendez offered condolences to the City of Duarte for the passing of their Mayor, Bryan Urias. He also
congratulated the City and the library for pulling off a successful Fall Festival.

Mayor Gonzales also congratulated the library and the City for hosting a wonderful Fall Festival that was well attended.
He commended Staff on their hard work.

He mentioned that Encouragement Church will be doing a drive thru event on November 20th to distribute Thanksgiving
meals to those in need.

Mayor Gonzales acknowledged the historical significance of the old Dalton Bakery that was recently torn down. The
building was 94 years old and he suggested commemorating the few older buildings left in the City.

On Saturday, November 6th and the City will be having a household hazardous waste event and a tree planting event,
hosted by the Azusa Beautiful Organization. On November 17th, the Azusa City Library will be having a Family Night
event. In addition, the Library will be having educational events in partnership with Azusa Pacific University.

Mayor Gonzales also advised residents to protect themselves against COVID-19.

SCHEDULED ITEMS – CITY COUNCIL

APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT TWENTY-SIX TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED FRANCHISE AGREEMENT
WITH ARKELIAN ENTERPRISES, INC. (DBA ATHENS SERVICES) FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SB 1383
REQUIREMENTS AND OTHER CONTRACTUAL ENHANCEMENTS.

City Manager Gonzalez provided an overview of the item and answered related question.

Moved by Mayor Pro-Tem Avila, seconded by Councilmember Mendez, and carried by unanimous vote of the Council to
approve the Twenty-sixth Amendment to the Amended and Restated Franchise Agreement with Araklian Enterprises, Inc
(dba Athens Services) to collect solid waste, recyclables, and organic waste in compliance with the requirements of SB
1383.
 AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: BECKWITH

Moved by Mayor Pro-Tem Avila, seconded by Councilmember Mendez, and carried by unanimous vote of the Council to
direct staff to initiate the Proposition 218 process for Public Hearing on December 13, 2021 to set refuse and organics
recycling rates effective January 1, 2022 and the next five fiscal years.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: BECKWITH

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion by Councilmember Alvarez to approve the Consent Calendar Items E-1 to E-8, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem
Avila, and carried by unanimous vote of the Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: BECKWITH

1. The minutes of the Regular Meeting of September 20, 2021 were approved as written.

2. Resolution No. 2021-C49 was adopted authorizing payments of warrants by the City dated October 14, 2021 through
  October 27 29, 2021 and approved.
3. Personnel Action Requests in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules and applicable
  Memorandum of Understanding(s) was approved.

4. The Plans and Specifications for CDBG Project 602307-21 was approved and the solicit of Notice of
  Inviting Bids for the CDBG Project 602307-21, Sidewalks and ADA Improvements was authorized.
5. The City Treasurer's Statement of Cash and Investment balances for the Month of August 2021 was received,
  reviewed, and filed.

6. The List of Purchase Orders issued in October 2021 with Contract Agreement executed by City Manager was
  received and filed.

7. Award a professional services agreement to Willdan for a total not-to-exceed $74,812, plus a 10% contingency for
  potential change orders as needed, for the Alosta Avenue Street Improvements Project; and Authorize the City
  Manager to execute a professional services agreement, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the
  City, was approved.

8. Approve the issuance of a purchase order to Anixter, Inc. in an amount of $349,663.78 for the purchase of
  Pad-mounted and Pole-mounted Transformers, was approved.

ADJOURNMENT

It was the consensus of the Council to adjourn the meeting in memory of Bryan Urias, Mayor City of Duarte and Ralph
Munoz, Lifelong Azusa Resident and those Azusans who we’ve lost to Covid-19.
